title: How Many Triangles Hide in This Hexagon? | AMC 8-Style Level 5

scenes.visual: The hexagon figure (bank SVG, redrawn large on a triangular lattice). Line 1: a few small triangles flash one at a time. Line 2: one size-2 triangle outline flashes, then one big size-3 triangle outline flashes (just a hint, no counts). Line 3: Vantee title card.
lines: This hexagon is cut into twenty-four little triangles. But that's not the whole story!
Bigger triangles are hiding in it too. Some of them are sneaky.
Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's hunt down every triangle.

scenes.visual: Question text left, hexagon right. Line 2: one hexagon side marked '2' (two small edges). Line 3: small triangles fill in light color briefly, label '24 small'. Line 4: tag 'any size'. Line 5: choice chips 24, 30, 32, 36, 38.
lines: Here's the question.
A regular hexagon has side length two.
It's cut into twenty-four small equilateral triangles.
How many triangles of any size are in the figure?
Here are the five choices.

scenes.visual: Line 1: one small triangle highlighted 'side 1'. Line 2: one size-2 up triangle (4 small ones) highlighted 'side 2'. Line 3: an up and a down small triangle side by side with arrows '▲ points up', '▼ points down'.
lines: Each little triangle has side one. Two small edges make a hexagon side.
We count triangles of every size, as long as their edges are drawn lines.
And watch the direction. Some triangles point up, and some point down.

scenes.visual: Pause card with countdown ring; hexagon and question visible.
lines: Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!

scenes.visual: A tally panel right: 'side 1', 'side 2', 'side 3'. Line 1: tag 'one size at a time'. Line 2: all 24 small triangles shade in, row by row (4 rows), tally 'side 1: 24'.
lines: Welcome back! Let's count one size at a time.
Side one is easy. Those are the twenty-four little triangles we were given.

scenes.visual: Line 1: one size-2 triangle (4 small, with a corner at the hexagon's centre) outlined. Line 2: the six 'wedge' size-2 triangles around the centre appear one by one (ONE outline moving to each spot, leaving faint ghosts, ×n counter to 6), alternating up/down. Line 3: tag 'all touch the centre with a corner'. Lines 4–5: a different size-2 triangle outlined whose side passes through the centre (centre dot at the middle of one of its sides). Line 6: the six of these appear one by one the same way, counter 6 more. Line 7: tally 'side 2: 6 + 6 = 12'. On line 6 each new one's far corner lands on a dot at the middle of a hexagon side.
lines: Side two is made of four small triangles.
Six of them fit around the center, like slices of a pizza.
Each slice has a corner right at the center.
But here's a sneaky one. None of its corners is at the center.
The center sits in the middle of one of its sides.
There are six of these too, each pointing to the middle of a hexagon side.
So side two gives six plus six, twelve triangles.

scenes.visual: Line 1: dots on the midpoints of the hexagon's six sides. Line 2: the up size-3 triangle joining three alternate midpoints draws itself. Line 3: the down size-3 triangle joining the other three midpoints. Lines 4–5: a side-4 base laid on the middle line, its apex poking 2 rows outside the hexagon, red ✗. Line 6: tally total '24 + 12 + 2 = 38' answer badge, chime at end, choice E highlighted.
lines: What about side three? Look at the middle of each side of the hexagon.
Join every other middle, and you get one big triangle pointing up.
Join the other three, and you get one pointing down. That's two.
Side four won't fit. Its bottom edge would need one of the long lines through the middle.
But only two rows fit above or below that line.
Twenty-four plus twelve plus two is thirty-eight. That's Choice E!

scenes.visual: Fresh hexagon. Line 1: tag 'count only ▲'. Line 2: the 12 up small triangles shade (down ones stay white): '12'. Line 3: the 6 up size-2 triangles appear one by one: '6'; then the 1 up size-3: '1'. Line 4: '12 + 6 + 1 = 19'. Line 5: the hexagon rotates 180° (half turn) and the shaded ▲ become ▼; '19 ▼ too'. Line 6: '2 × 19 = 38'. Line 7: small text 'use symmetry'.
lines: Time for a clever shortcut. Count only the triangles that point up.
Twelve of the small ones point up.
Six of the side-two triangles point up, and one of the big ones.
That's twelve plus six plus one, nineteen.
Now turn the hexagon upside down. It looks the same, but every up triangle now points down!
So there are nineteen pointing down too. Two times nineteen is thirty-eight.
When would you pick this way? When the shape looks the same upside down.

scenes.visual: Choice chips with the sums under them. Line 1: chip A '24 = small only'. Line 2: chip B '24 + 6 = 30' with the 6 pizza slices shown. Line 3: chip C '24 + 6 + 2 = 32' with only up size-2 ones shown. Line 4: chip D '24 + 12 = 36' with the two big ones crossed out. Line 5: chip E '38' green.
lines: Now the traps. Choice A, twenty-four, counts only the little triangles.
Choice B, thirty, is what you'd get if you found only the six pizza slices of side two.
Choice C, thirty-two, counts side-two triangles in only one direction.
Choice D, thirty-six, forgets the two big triangles that stretch across the hexagon.
Count every size, in both directions, and you get thirty-eight.

scenes.visual: New figure: an equilateral triangle of side 4, cut into 16 small triangles (lattice lines drawn). Tag 'how many triangles of any size?'.
lines: Ready for a challenge? This big triangle has side four. It's cut into sixteen small triangles.
How many triangles of any size are in it?

scenes.visual: Pause card, countdown, variant figure visible.
lines: Pause the video, and go for it!

scenes.visual: Tally per line: 'side 1: 16'; 'side 2: 6 ▲' (shown one by one) then the single ▼ side-2 triangle in the middle highlighted, '+1 = 7'; 'side 3: 3'; 'side 4: 1'; answer badge '16 + 7 + 3 + 1 = 27' chime at end of that line.
lines: Let's check. Side one: the sixteen small ones.
Side two: six point up. And don't miss the sneaky one in the middle, pointing down. That's seven.
Side three: three of them, one in each corner.
Side four: the whole triangle.
Sixteen plus seven plus three plus one is twenty-seven!
If you got twenty-seven, outstanding hunting!

scenes.visual: Summary card: 'size by size', '▲ and ▼', 'symmetry can halve the work'.
lines: Here's the big idea to remember.
Count the triangles one size at a time, and check both directions, up and down.
If the shape looks the same upside down, count one direction and double it.
I'm Vantee. Keep hunting, and I'll see you next time!
